question_text: July Exam Memo 2009 Grade 11 History Question 1-Source Based Analysis Question-The Arms race Each side anxious to show the other side up and to be the guilty party (propaganda), both sides keen to find out what the other side was up to (intelligence). 2x2=(4) Human spies and technological equipment. (2) Nuclear deterrent=nuclear capability prevents countries from going to war because of its destructive power. PLEASE DON’T COUNT OUT THE WORDS, JUST DON’T WRITE TOO MUCH! (3) By this stage the USSR also has the atom bomb, he is aware that this makes for “an uneasy peace”, but he is more than likely referring to the Truman Doctrine and the Marshall Plan to be used to contain Russia, using aid and the threat of weapons should allow for America to keep the USSR at bay. (6) MY MISTAKE IN ASKING YOU TO DECIDE WHICH IS WHICH-YOU JUST HAD TO EXPLAIN THE MESSAGE OF EACH CARTOON-APOLOGIES! They are both Soviet cartoons-Source C is a strong Soviet perception that the USA, shown by the dollar signs on the guard’s shoulders, is surprised that the USSR has developed the atom bomb. The US “atomic monopoly” has been burst and the USA and the USSR is now on an equal footing. Source D takes a very anti-Western stance, puts Nazi Germany and Western capitalism in the same coach. NATO, SEATO and CENTO were all set up to deal with a perceived Soviet threat; according to this cartoonist it is the West that is fuelling the arms race. He believes that the West is very hostile and provocative, but the West is quick to blame the USSR for the tension. (10) Soviet cartoon is saying that the U-2 spy plane is powerful, invasive, threatening and underhanded. (3) It is a violation of their airspace and privacy, it cannot be shot down. 2x2=(4) They believed communism was a huge threat aimed at world wide
